title: Sequential Grid Path Cover
summary: Input is grid and k. Start at any cell. Visit all cells exactly once by side-adjacent moves, encountering nonzero labels in order 1 through k. Return m*n zero-based [row,column] pairs, or [] if no such path exists. The statement specifies validity, not a prescribed construction or a separate closed-form impossibility criterion.
officialConstraints: Official-page confirmation pending. See constraintsReportedBySource for the bounds in the community reproduction.
exampleStatus: No source examples copied; independently author and check teaching examples.
clarification: Authored example: grid=[[2,0,1]], k=2 permits [[0,2],[0,1],[0,0]]. Grid [[1,3,2]], k=3 is impossible: a path covering a single row must traverse it from an endpoint, and neither direction visits labels in order.
constraintsReportedBySource: 1<=m,n<=5; 1<=k<=m*n; entries 0..k; each label 1..k occurs exactly once.
verificationStatus: community-reproduction-read; official text not independently confirmed
